title: Maximum number of spanning trees in bipartite graphs with a given diameter
summary: The number of spanning trees is a classical graph invariant and an important measure of network reliability, as it counts the minimal connected spanning substructures that can maintain communication in a network. Let $\mathcal{B}(n,d)$ be the set of connected bipartite graphs of order $n$ and diameter $d$. Motivated by reliability design problems for bipartite network models with fixed order and diameter, this paper determines all graphs with the maximum number of spanning trees in $\mathcal{B}(n,d)$.
